Candidate mechanism, from code reading plus one measurement; not yet reproduced with an instrumented sweep. (1) compact_all_cli builds one position->commit map before locking (_sweep_position_map). If that returns None/empty (git failure, or map misses), the fold path calls _build_authorship_ledger (src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py) INSIDE the store write lock. For each signed event with no map hit it runs authorship.resolve_event_commit (ticket-scoped git log --full-history), and if that returns None, authorship.resolve_position_commit (src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py): a STORE-WIDE 'git log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames -- *<position>-*.json' with a 30 s timeout. (3) The between-ticket yield (_sweep_should_yield -> write_lock_is_busy) only sees a CURRENT HOLDER, not a writer waiting to acquire, so it cannot shorten a long single-ticket fold. Proposed next steps: instrument a sweep against a copy of the store to count map misses and lock hold time per ticket; fix by never running unbounded git walks under the lock (resolve commits before taking it, or store null and fill later) and bounding the in-lock work; regression test with a fake git that sleeps.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
During the comment-remediation epic on 2026-10-22 PDT, multiple MCP tracker writes (leaf close, progress comments, and an inventory edit) timed out after 91–181 seconds waiting for the tickets write lock. The holder was `op=compact-sweep`. Read-only SSM checks found two successive detached sweeps running for 33:46 and 11:00 respectively, with `git log --full-history` children under them. Targeted SIGTERM to each optional sweep process group released the lock; the next leaf close and comment writes succeeded. Rebar's lock error says interrupted sweep events stay live. This is a repeated write outage, not a proven root cause.

## Reproduction (2026-10-24, current main; no mocks of git)
Seed a store, commit signed events, then create a side branch and an "evil merge" whose merge commit adds a signed event file that no non-merge commit ever added. Run `compact_all_cli`. The sweep's position map is built with `--no-merges` (`authorship_resolution.build_position_commit_map`), so that event misses it, and `_build_authorship_ledger` then runs `authorship.resolve_event_commit` and `authorship.resolve_position_commit` while `.ticket-write.lock.d` exists: both resolvers were observed running under the store write lock. The existing test `test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` passes anyway because it watches only the two map builders, not these resolvers.

## Measurement
On the operator host's tickets clone (300,142 commits, host load about 12) one store-wide `git log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames -- *<position>-*.json` took 140 s and 142 s on two runs; `resolve_position_commit` times out at 30 s. Not measured: how often the production server's sweep misses the map.

## Root cause
`_compact_locked` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`) takes the store write lock, then builds the authorship ledger. Each signed event missing from the sweep's map falls back to up to two unbounded `git log` walks inside the lock. The between-ticket yield (`_sweep_should_yield`) sees only a current holder and cannot shorten one ticket's fold.

## Approach
1. In `compact_txn.py` add `preresolve_unmapped_positions(ticket_dir, tracker, repo_root, position_commits)`: list the ticket's signed event positions absent from the map and resolve each with the existing resolvers, returning a COPY of the map with one entry per miss. Every outcome that today yields no commit gets the value `""`: both resolvers catch every exception, including the 30 s `TimeoutExpired`, and return `None`, so a timeout is indistinguishable from "no commit" at that API, and today's in-lock path already persists null when both fail. A timed-out position is deliberately NOT left absent: that would send the same walk back through the in-lock fallback, which is the defect. On a clone this size timeouts are the expected case, so the persisted ledger equals today's, and only the lock time changes.
2. Call it from `_sweep_one_ticket` in `compact.py`, before `compact_cli` takes the lock, only when a sweep map exists.
3. In `_build_authorship_ledger`, a position present in the map is final. `""` exists ONLY as the in-map "already attempted" marker and is never persisted: the extracted helper turns it into `None`, so the ledger entry carries JSON `null` for `commit_sha` exactly as today, `verify_authorship._verify_signed` (which branches on `commit_sha is None`) sees the same value, and no walk runs under the lock. A position absent from the map (an event that arrived after pre-resolution) keeps today's fallback.
4. Extract the commit-resolution step into a helper so `_build_authorship_ledger` (complexity 9, ceiling 15) does not grow.
The persisted ledger is unchanged: the same commit is found, only outside the lock.

## Scope
In scope: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`, `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py`. `compact_rebuild.py` also calls `_build_authorship_ledger` (the fsck rebuild path); it passes no map, so the new sentinel never applies there and its behaviour is unchanged, which a test pins. Out of scope: the `--no-merges` map itself, the single-ticket close path, the 30 s resolver timeout, and the lock implementation.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py tests/unit/test_compact_trigger.py tests/unit/test_compact_crash_atomicity.py -q
make verify
```
New tests: (a) merge-only event: no resolver runs while the lock directory exists, and the ledger commit equals the one found by a direct resolver call; (b) an unresolvable position (resolvers return None) persists a null commit with no resolver call under the lock; (c) the ledger is identical with and without pre-resolution, and a double-miss persists JSON null (not an empty string) with the same `verify_authorship` verdict as before; (d) an event added after pre-resolution still resolves through the in-lock fallback; (e) a resolver that times out during pre-resolution persists null with no in-lock walk; (f) `_build_authorship_ledger` called with no map (the rebuild path) behaves as before. Failure case: (a) and (b) fail on main with the resolver names listed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With a merge-only signed event, no history walk (map builder or resolver) runs while the store lock is held (checked: new test, which fails on main naming `resolve_event_commit` and `resolve_position_commit`).
- [ ] The persisted authorship ledger is identical to the pre-change ledger for the same store (checked: new equality test).
- [ ] A position unresolvable outside the lock, including one whose resolver timed out, is persisted as JSON null (never an empty string) without any in-lock walk, and verify-identity gives the same verdict as before (checked: new tests).
- [ ] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).

## Follow-up
Whether the production server's sweep actually hits the map-miss path, and how often, is a read-only server check tracked in its own task.
